assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing rests on chemistry: reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis and, in parallel, massively parallel pyrosequencing. It transformed biology and medicine and has had durable, quantifiable impact that is hard to overstate.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule/cluster concept; Rothberg is the most defensible third as the first commercial massively parallel platform. Ju (terminators), Mayer (colony amplification) and others make the three-person limit contentious.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of near-universal adoption, with independent confirmation and no doubt about stability. Recognition is fully timely or even overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among competing technology lineages (reversible terminators, pyrosequencing, polony/cluster amplification) is unresolved.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as biology and instrumentation; I rely on recollection of the history, not independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is a fundamental biochemical-energy-conversion problem: how a metalloenzyme drives electron and proton transfer to reduce N2. Structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor, including the central light atom, with kinetic mechanism, make a mechanism visible, which is the kind of work I value most.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the first structures and the cofactor and electron-transfer analysis; Einsle resolved the high-resolution cofactor and its interstitial atom; Seefeldt and Dean (and Ribbe) built the kinetic and mechanistic framework. A fair trio exists but excludes real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Structural picture is well confirmed. The catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction is still not settled, so the story is mature for structure and incomplete for mechanism.
uncertainties: Substrate-binding and the E4 intermediate mechanism remain debated.
Priority and weighting between structural and biochemical/kinetic contributors is unclear; the expert reports should settle it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer gives a general physical framework for concerted proton and electron movement, which underlies respiration, photosynthesis, and molecular electrocatalysis. It ties theory, kinetics and synthetic models together and has real, lasting conceptual influence across chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Mayer established concerted PCET and bond-weakening/thermochemical concepts in synthetic systems; Nocera developed PCET in model systems and artificial photosynthesis; Hammes-Schiffer supplied the theoretical formulation. Meyer's early contributions complicate a clean three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally and theoretically mature and widely confirmed, though its impact is distributed over several fields and this is a field rather than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Risk that this is a line of work rather than a single attributable discovery, and that priority versus Meyer and others is disputed.
I may overweight it because of my own research area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced protein degradation, via PROTACs and molecular glue degraders including the mechanism of thalidomide action through cereblon, created a new therapeutic modality and a new way to probe biology. Strong chemical-biology novelty with clinical consequence.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and built the PROTAC concept; the cereblon identification (Handa, Ito) explains glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim also contributed. Up to eight names; the three-laureate limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still maturing; mechanistic basis is solid but long-term clinical impact is not yet established, so slight prematurity.
uncertainties: Attribution split between PROTAC inventors and molecular-glue mechanism discoverers is unresolved.
Clinical track record is still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand cleavage by pairing deaminase chemistry with a programmable DNA-binding protein. It is a clear, original design principle with large downstream use in research and therapy.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees on cytosine and adenine base editors. A single-laureate recommendation is the cleanest, but possible pairing with the prime-editing work should be considered.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old; robust independent reproduction and first clinical use, but long-term safety and impact are still developing, so likely a little early.
uncertainties: Whether recognition should come as part of a broader editing prize.
Overlap with the Nobel already given for CRISPR-Cas9 chemistry-category recognition raises questions of timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale proteomics by mass spectrometry changed how cellular proteins and their modifications are measured; it is a foundational analytical capability across life science.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, quantitative and large-scale workflows), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative methods, isotope tags) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT and database search) are the main figures; Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong. Credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively validated, but its recognition may be seen as partly covered by earlier ionization-method prizes.
uncertainties: A rich field with many contributors and no single clear discovery.
Overlap with the earlier mass-spectrometry Nobel for ionization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules electrically through nanopores combines biophysics and chemistry and gave a new sequencing mode, with long reads and direct detection of modifications.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz proposed and demonstrated nanopore detection; Bayley engineered protein pores; Akeson demonstrated strand-level reading and the enzyme-ratcheting approach. Priority disputes make credit hard.
assessment.maturity: Technology is commercial and broadly used, with independent validation; accuracy and chemistry continue to evolve.
uncertainties: Contested priority among the founding concept, protein engineering and sequencing implementation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allows structures from tiny crystals before radiation damage and time-resolved structural movies of reactions. This fits my interest in visualizing dynamic processes in biological catalysis in physical terms.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme (with Spence, who is not on the supplied list) and Schlichting made the core demonstrations; Hajdu's early conceptual role cannot be recognized if he is deceased. The supplied credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Proof of principle and time-resolved results are established, but broad chemical impact and independence from a few facilities are still limited, so a bit early.
uncertainties: Missing key contributor and difficult allocation given the list.
Uncertain how many mechanistic results have transformed chemistry so far.
